question: An MFM contract explicitly credits work RVUs. Which measure belongs in that productivity ledger?
options: Total RVUs including practice expense
Work RVUs credited under the contract
The amount the payer collected from the patient
The Medicare conversion factor
rationales: Total RVUs include components outside this stated contract.
Correct: the contract specifies work RVUs and its crediting rules.
Patient payments are collections, not work RVUs.
The conversion factor converts adjusted RVUs to a fee-schedule amount.

question: A fictional contract pays $55 per credited wRVU with no threshold. A visit receives 2 wRVUs. What compensation follows from these assumptions?
rationales: This substitutes the rounded Medicare CF for the contract rate.
This uses the slide’s separate payment example.
Correct: 2 × $55 = $110. The assumptions exclude thresholds or other adjustments.
This credits one wRVU rather than two.

question: A Medicaid patient is referred for an MFM opinion about maternal disease. What is the next coding step?
options: Automatically use an outpatient consultation code
Use the highest new-patient code
Apply Medicare consultation policy to every Medicaid plan
Check this payer’s code recognition and documentation requirements
rationales: Referral alone does not establish payer recognition.
Neither patient status nor level is established by the referral.
Medicare policy is not a universal Medicaid rule.
Correct: identify the plan’s policy before selecting the E/M family.

question: A stable patient’s chart carries a high-risk pregnancy diagnosis. What best supports office E/M level selection?
options: Documented MDM or qualifying clinician time
The high-risk diagnosis alone
The length of the copied problem list
The number of ultrasound images
rationales: Correct: evaluate the work supported by today’s record.
A risk label does not establish a complete E/M level.
Copied text is not evidence of work addressed today.
Image count is not an office E/M leveling criterion.

question: An MFM clinician spends 35 qualifying minutes on E/M and 10 additional minutes on separately billed scan interpretation. How much time enters the E/M calculation?
options: 45 minutes
10 minutes
35 minutes
All time the patient spends in the clinic
rationales: This double counts separately reported work.
This counts only the excluded service.
Correct: count the 35 eligible E/M minutes.
Waiting and staff time do not become clinician E/M time.

question: After a fetal anatomy scan, the physician only provides the explanation ordinarily included with the imaging service. What is the best billing conclusion?
options: Every scan also supports a level-3 visit
A separate E/M service is not established by this description
Modifier 25 creates a separate visit
A second diagnosis guarantees E/M payment
rationales: No independent E/M work has been established.
Correct: routine scan-related work alone does not show separate E/M.
A modifier describes work; it does not create it.
Diagnosis count cannot substitute for a separate service.

question: Another practice provides routine prenatal care while MFM manages a complication. How should the team assess billing?
options: All MFM services are included in the other practice’s global fee
All MFM services are separately payable
Use a global delivery code for every MFM visit
Clarify care responsibilities and payer/global-package rules
rationales: This may conceal eligible separate work.
This may improperly unbundle care.
The MFM visit does not establish delivery/global services.
Correct: determine which services were supplied and how the payer treats them.

question: An MFM claim was paid correctly, but the clinician’s production report lacks credit. What should happen first?
options: Reconcile rendering identity and contract credit rules
Submit the paid claim again
Add modifier 59 to generate credit
Assume the payer owes more
rationales: Correct: investigate the internal attribution mismatch.
Duplicate submission does not fix the productivity ledger.
Modifier 59 does not assign employment credit.
A crediting issue does not establish payer underpayment.

question: The hospital furnished ultrasound equipment and acquisition. The MFM physician furnished only interpretation and report. Which approach is appropriate?
options: Bill global imaging because the report is signed
Bill only the technical component
Assess professional-component billing under the arrangement
Add modifier 25 to the imaging code
rationales: Signing does not establish entitlement to both components.
The physician furnished professional interpretation, not acquisition.
Correct: verify component eligibility and the billing arrangement.
Modifier 25 describes qualifying E/M, not imaging ownership.

question: FGR ultrasound is followed by a separately documented management visit. What is the strongest approach to E/M billing?
options: Add modifier 25 without reviewing the note
Support the separate service and verify payer modifier requirements
Include scan interpretation time in E/M
Use a different diagnosis solely to obtain payment
rationales: The record must support separate work.
Correct: the service and policy determine the claim.
Separately reported scan time must be excluded.
Diagnosis manipulation does not establish eligibility.

question: A physician co-signs an APP’s Medicare office note but performs no additional work. Incident-to requirements have not been established. What is correct?
options: The signature alone supports physician billing
This is automatically a split/shared office visit
The highest clinician credential determines billing
The team must establish a valid pathway from the actual work
rationales: A signature alone does not establish the required service or supervision conditions.
Medicare office visits are not split/shared visits.
Credential hierarchy does not replace billing requirements.
Correct: assess direct APP billing or another pathway only if its conditions are met.

question: A fetal imaging claim has a procedure-to-procedure edit. What is the best next action?
options: Check the current pair, modifier indicator and documented circumstances
Append modifier 59 to every denied imaging line
Assume separate diagnoses override the edit
Replace the performed service with a higher-valued code
rationales: Correct: determine whether a supported modifier exception is available.
A denial is not evidence of distinct services.
Separate diagnoses alone do not satisfy modifier requirements.
Code the work performed, not a payment target.

question: An enrolled MFM NP personally performs a medically necessary office visit within scope. Incident-to criteria are not met. What pathway may be available?
options: No professional service can be billed
Only billing through the physician’s NPI
Direct NP billing if the service meets payer requirements
Automatic global maternity billing
rationales: Failure of incident-to eligibility does not eliminate direct billing eligibility.
A physician NPI is not universally required.
Correct: eligible personally furnished NP services can be directly billed.
This encounter does not establish a global maternity service.

question: An NP evaluates a new concern during established diabetes follow-up. The physician has not addressed that concern. What should the NP do about billing?
options: Reassess incident-to eligibility and document the actual work
Use incident-to because the patient is established
Obtain only a co-signature and assume eligibility
Ignore the new concern to preserve the original billing plan
rationales: Correct: evaluate the new problem clinically and verify the appropriate billing pathway.
Patient status alone is insufficient.
A co-signature does not establish the required treatment involvement.
Patient needs determine care; the billing plan must follow it.

question: Which statement best describes Medicare’s typical direct professional-service allowed amounts for NPs/PAs and CNMs?
options: Every APP receives 85% under every payer
NP/PA generally 85%; eligible CNM services 100% of the physician fee-schedule basis
All receive 100% if a physician is in the building
The percentage equals the clinician’s take-home pay
rationales: Both profession and payer matter.
Correct: these are Medicare allowed-amount rules, not universal payer or salary rules.
Availability alone does not change the direct-billing percentage.
Employment compensation and allowed amounts are different measures.

question: An APP and physician from the same group share an eligible hospital outpatient E/M encounter. What determines the Medicare split/shared billing clinician?
options: Who opened the chart first
Who has the higher salary
Who co-signed last
Who performed the substantive portion under the applicable rule
rationales: Chart-opening order is not the criterion.
Compensation does not determine the renderer.
Signature sequence does not establish substantive work.
Correct: verify substantive MDM or more than half of distinct time for eligible noncritical E/M, plus documentation and FS requirements.
